title: Calculator Line
statement: A simple calculator reads a line with non-negative integers, the operators +, −, * and /, and spaces. Multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction; division keeps only the whole part (rounding towards zero). Return the result. Every intermediate result fits in a 32-bit integer.
constraints: the line is a valid expression

answerKey.pattern: One pass with a stack of terms (or a running sum and the last term)
keyPoints: Read a number, then act on the operator before it
+ pushes the number, − pushes its negative
* and / combine with the last term on the stack; the answer is the sum
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(n), or O(1) with a running sum and last term
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Two passes: first * and /, then + and −: also O(n)

hints: Why can't you add as you go from left to right?
A later * or / binds tighter than a + before it.
Keep the last term separate: on * or / update it; on + or − add it to the sum and start a new term.
